## R Markdown

This is an R Markdown document. Markdown is a simple formatting syntax for authoring HTML, PDF, and MS Word documents. For more details on using R Markdown see <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com>.

When you click the **Knit** button a document will be generated that includes both content as well as the output of any embedded R code chunks within the document. You can embed an R code chunk like this:

Task 1

```{r cars}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyverse)

orderItems = read.csv("order_items.csv")
products = read.csv("products.csv")

frequencyPrice = orderItems %>% count(price)
highestFrequency = head(frequencyPrice)
lowestFrequency = tail(frequencyPrice)

meanPrice = mean(orderItems$price)
medianPrice = median(orderItems$price)

ggplot(data = frequencyPrice) + geom_histogram(mapping = aes(x = price), binwidth = 100, na.rm = TRUE) + labs(title = "Histogram of Item Price", x = "Item Price", y = "Frequency")


productsOrderItems = orderItems %>% inner_join(products, by = "product_id")

ggplot(data = productsOrderItems) + geom_point(mapping = aes(x = product_weight_g, y = freight_value)) +
  geom_smooth(
    mapping = aes(x = product_weight_g, y = freight_value), method = "lm", na.rm = TRUE) + labs(title = "Scatter Plot of Product Weight vs Freight Value", x = "Product Weight", y = "Freight Value")

corWeightFreightValue = cor.test(productsOrderItems$product_weight_g, productsOrderItems$freight_value, method = "pearson")

```

## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}
plot(pressure)
```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.
